{{Short description|Video game integrating cryptocurrency or NFTs}}
{{pp-semi-indef|small=yes}}
[[Video game]]s can include elements that use [[blockchain]] technologies, including [[cryptocurrency|cryptocurrencies]] and [[non-fungible token]]s (NFTs), often as a form of [[video game monetization|monetization]]. These elements typically allow players to trade in-game items for cryptocurrency, or represent in-game items with NFTs. Blockchain games have existed since 2017, gaining wider attention from the [[video game industry]] in 2021, when several [[AAA (video game industry)|AAA publishers]] expressed an intent to include this technology in the future. Players, developers, and game companies have criticized the use of blockchain technology in video games for being exploitative, environmentally unsustainable, and unnecessary.

A subset of these games are also known as '''play-to-earn games''' because they include systems that allow players to earn cryptocurrency through gameplay.

== Concept ==
Blockchains have been used by game developers and publishers as a tool for [[video game monetization]]. Many video games offer in-game customization options, such as changes to a character's appearance, improved  equipment, or other options. In some [[Games as a service|live-service games]], players can also trade with other players, either directly or via in-game currency. Trading of virtual items for money may be illegal in some countries where this is classified as illegal/under-age [[gambling]], [[money laundering]], or [[securities fraud]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cloward |first1=J. Gregory |last2=Abarbanel |first2=Brett L. |title=In-Game Currencies, Skin Gambling, and the Persistent Threat of Money Laundering in Video Games |journal=UNLV Gaming Law Journal |date=1 March 2020 |volume=10 |issue=1 |pages=105 |url=https://scholars.law.unlv.edu/glj/vol10/iss1/6/}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Qiao |first1=Diana |title=This is Not a Game: Blockchain Regulation and Its Application to Video Games |journal=Northern Illinois University Law Review |date=1 May 2020 |volume=40 |issue=2 |pages=176–226 |url=https://huskiecommons.lib.niu.edu/niulr/vol40/iss2/4/ |issn=0734-1490}}</ref> This has led to [[gray market]] activity such as [[skin gambling]], and publishers often attempt to prohibit players from earning real-world funds from games for legal reasons.<ref name="Verge-Valve">{{cite news |last1=Clark |first1=Mitchell |title=Valve bans blockchain games and NFTs on Steam, Epic will try to make it work |url=https://www.theverge.com/2021/10/15/22728425/valve-steam-blockchain-nft-crypto-ban-games-age-of-rust |access-date=8 November 2021 |work=The Verge |date=15 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lopez-Gonzalez |first1=Hibai |last2=Petrotta |first2=Brian |title=Gambling-like digital assets and gambling severity: a correlational study with U.S. sports bettors consuming cryptocurrencies, NFTs, and fan tokens |journal=International Gambling Studies |date=3 May 2024 |volume=24 |issue=2 |pages=341–356 |doi=10.1080/14459795.2023.2279125}}</ref> To avoid these regulations, blockchain games allow players to trade in-game items for cryptocurrency, which can then be exchanged for money via a cryptocurrency exchange.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Greer |first1=Nancy |last2=Rockloff |first2=Matthew |last3=Hing |first3=Nerilee |last4=Browne |first4=Matthew |last5=King |first5=Daniel L. |title=Skin Gambling Contributes to Gambling Problems and Harm After Controlling for Other Forms of Traditional Gambling |journal=Journal of Gambling Studies |date=1 March 2023 |volume=39 |issue=1 |pages=225–247 |doi=10.1007/s10899-022-10111-z |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10899-022-10111-z |language=en |issn=1573-3602|pmc=9981708 }}</ref><ref name="inverse blockchain games">{{cite web | url = https://www.inverse.com/gaming/blockchain-games-online-gaming | title = Blockchain Games Twist The Fundamentals Of Online Gaming | first = Mo | last = Mozuch | date = 29 April 2021 | accessdate = 4 November 2021 | work = [[Inverse (website)|Inverse]] }}</ref>

== History ==
One of the first best-known games to use blockchain technologies was ''[[CryptoKitties]]'', launched by Axiom Zen in November 2017 for personal computers. A player would purchase NFTs with [[Ethereum]] cryptocurrency, each NFT consisting of a [[virtual pet]] that the player could breed with others to create offspring with combined traits as new NFTs.<ref>{{Cite news |date=22 February 2018 |title=Internet firms try their luck at blockchain games |work=[[Asia Times]] |url=https://asiatimes.com/article/internet-firms-try-luck-blockchain-games/ |access-date=28 February 2018}}</ref><ref name="inverse blockchain games" /> The game made headlines in December 2017 when one virtual pet sold for more than {{US$|100,000}}.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Evelyn Cheng |date=6 December 2017 |title=Meet CryptoKitties, the $100,000 digital beanie babies epitomizing the cryptocurrency mania |publisher=[[CNBC]] |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2017/12/06/meet-cryptokitties-the-new-digital-beanie-babies-selling-for-100k.html |url-status=live |access-date=28 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181120115903/https://www.cnbc.com/2017/12/06/meet-cryptokitties-the-new-digital-beanie-babies-selling-for-100k.html |archive-date=20 November 2018}}</ref> ''CryptoKitties'' also exposed scalability problems for games on Ethereum when it created significant congestion on the Ethereum network shortly after its launch, with approximately 30% of all Ethereum transactions at the time being for the game, and with the congestion delaying players' transactions. Axiom Zen feared that Ethereum would further struggle after they launched the mobile version of the game, particularly with an influx of users from [[China]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Laignee Barron |date=13 February 2018 |title=CryptoKitties is Going Mobile. Can Ethereum Handle the Traffic? |work=[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]] |url=http://fortune.com/2018/02/13/cryptokitties-ethereum-ios-launch-china-ether/ |url-status=live |access-date=30 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181028041832/http://fortune.com/2018/02/13/cryptokitties-ethereum-ios-launch-china-ether/ |archive-date=28 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=12 May 2017 |title=CryptoKitties craze slows down transactions on Ethereum |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-42237162 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180112143517/http://www.bbc.com/news/technology-42237162 |archive-date=12 January 2018}}</ref>

''The Sandbox'' is a platform that bought the brandname of [[The Sandbox (2012 video game)|a 2012 crafting game of the same name]], in 2018. Players could make in-game items by using the game's toolbox and then sell them, using a game-specific cryptocurrency, to others who could display them in their virtual landscapes.<ref name="inverse blockchain games" />

''[[Axie Infinity]]'', released in 2018 by Sky Mavis, is an example of a "play-to-earn" game, where the game incentivizes players to purchase and then improve NFTs through in-game activities which are then resold to other players by the publisher, with the player receiving compensation for their work. In the Philippines, where the game was most popular, some players were able to earn enough to pay their cost of living by playing and participating in the game's financial structure.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Nunley |first=Christian |date=14 May 2021 |title=People in the Philippines are earning cryptocurrency during the pandemic by playing a video game |work=CNBC |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/05/14/people-in-philippines-earn-cryptocurrency-playing-nft-video-game-axie-infinity.html |access-date=8 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-12-07/play-to-earn-crypto-gaming-apps-surpass-defi-in-user-popularity | title = Crypto Play-to-Earn 'GameFi' Apps Surpass DeFi in User Popularity | first = Olga | last=  Kharif | date = 7 December 2021 | accessdate = 30 December 2021 | work = [[Bloomberg News]] }}</ref> However, following an early 2022 hack which saw over $600 million stolen from ''Axie Infinity''{{'s}} publisher, the game saw a large drop in players and the game's economy was impacted.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.gamesradar.com/play-to-earn-workers-abandon-hacked-nft-game-stranding-digital-landlords/ | title = 'Play-to-earn' workers abandon hacked NFT game, stranding digital 'landlords' | first  = Austin | last = Wood | date = 12 April 2022 | accessdate=  13 April 2022 | work = [[GamesRadar]] }}</ref> Sky Mavis removed references to "play-to-earn" on its websites and marketing as its tokens plummeted in value.<ref name="Bloomberg">{{Cite web |last=Brustein |first=Joshua |date=10 June 2022 |title=A Billion-Dollar Crypto Gaming Startup Promised Riches and Delivered Disaster |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2022-06-10/axie-infinity-axs-crypto-game-promised-nft-riches-gave-ruin |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220610135130/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2022-06-10/axie-infinity-axs-crypto-game-promised-nft-riches-gave-ruin |archive-date=10 June 2022 |access-date=10 June 2022 |website=Bloomberg }}</ref>

By the early 2020s there had not been a breakout success in video games using blockchain. Such games tended to focus on using blockchain for speculation instead of more traditional forms of gameplay, and this offers limited appeal to most players. Such games also represent a high risk to investors as their revenues can be difficult to predict.<ref name="inverse blockchain games" /> However, limited successes of some games, such as ''Axie Infinity'' during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], and increasing corporate interest in [[metaverse]] content, refueled interest in the area of GameFi—a term describing the intersection of video games and financing, typically backed by blockchain currency—in the second half of 2021.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2021-10-30/what-is-the-metaverse-where-crypto-nft-capitalism-collide-in-games-like-axie | title = Into the Metaverse: Where Crypto, Gaming and Capitalism Collide | first1 = Charlie | last1 = Wells | first2 = Misrylena | last2 = Egkolfopoulou | date = 30 October 2021 | accessdate = 11 November 2021 | work = [[Bloomberg News]] }}</ref> By the end of 2021, several major publishers, including [[Ubisoft]], [[Electronic Arts]], [[Take Two Interactive]], and [[Square Enix]], stated that blockchain and NFT-based games were under serious consideration for their companies in the future.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2021/11/big-name-publishers-see-nfts-as-a-big-part-of-gamings-future/ | title = Big-name publishers see NFTs as a big part of gaming's future | first = Kyle | last = Orland | date = 4 November 2021 | accessdate = 4 November 2021 | work = [[Ars Technica]] }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/square-enix-says-it-hopes-nfts-and-blockchain-become-a-major-trend-in-games/ | title = Square Enix says it hopes NFTs and blockchain become 'a major trend' in games | first = Andy | last = Robinson | date = 1 January 2022 | accessdate = 1 January 2022 | work = [[Video Games Chronicle]] }}</ref>

In October 2021, [[Valve Corporation]] banned blockchain games, including those using cryptocurrency and NFTs, from being hosted on its [[Steam (service)|Steam]] digital storefront service, which is widely used for personal computer gaming. The company said this was an extension of their policy banning games that offer in-game items with real-world value. Valve's prior history with [[gambling]], specifically [[skin gambling]], was speculated to be a factor in the decision to ban blockchain games.<ref name=pcgamer /> Valve's CEO [[Gabe Newell]] explained in a later interview that while he believed blockchain technology was legitimate, the company felt there were too many bad actors in the market at the time to allow cryptocurrency or NFTs onto Steam. Newell said, "The ways in which it has been utilised are currently all pretty sketchy. And you sort of want to stay away from that."<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2022-02-25-gabe-newell-explains-why-steam-banned-nfts | title = Gabe Newell explains why Steam banned NFTs | first = Martin | last = Robinson | date = 25 February 2022 | accessdate = 5 March 2022 | work = [[Eurogamer]] }}</ref> Journalists and players responded positively to Valve's decision, as blockchain and NFT games have a reputation for scams and fraud among most PC gamers,<ref name="Verge-Valve" /><ref name=pcgamer>{{cite news |last1=Knoop |first1=Joseph |title=Steam bans all games with NFTs or cryptocurrency |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/steam-bans-nfts-cryptocurrencies-blockchain/ |access-date=8 November 2021 |work=PC Gamer |date=15 October 2021 }}</ref> while blockchain game publishers and developers urged Valve to reconsider their position.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://venturebeat.com/2021/10/26/29-blockchain-game-studios-and-groups-blast-valve-for-nft-games-ban/ | title = 29 blockchain game studios and groups blast Valve for NFT games ban |first=  Dean | last = Takahashi | date = 26 October 2021 | accessdate = 11 November 2021 | work = [[Venture Beat]] }}</ref> [[Epic Games]]'s CEO [[Tim Sweeney]] said in the wake of Valve's refusal that the [[Epic Games Store]] would be open to accepting blockchain games which followed relevant laws and regulations, although Sweeney noted that Epic did not use such technology at the time.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.theverge.com/2021/10/15/22729050/epic-game-store-open-to-blockchain-cryptocurrency-nft-games | title= Epic says it's 'open' to blockchain games after Steam bans them | first=  Mitchell | last =Clark | date= 15 October 2021 | accessdate = 11 November 2021 | work = [[The Verge]] }}</ref>

In December 2021, Ubisoft announced the Ubisoft Quartz program, based on the [[proof of stake]] [[Tezos]] cryptocurrency, which Ubisoft claimed was more [[Energy conservation|energy efficient]]. Quartz allows players to purchase and sell "Digits", which are in-game character customization items. The service launched with items in ''[[Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Breakpoint]]''.<ref>{{cite web|last=Price|first=Reneta|date=7 December 2021|title=Ubisoft First Major Pub To Befoul Own Game With NFTs|url=https://kotaku.com/ubisoft-first-major-pub-to-befoul-own-game-with-nfts-1848176813|work=[[Kotaku]]|accessdate=7 December 2021}}</ref> On the same day, ''[[Ars Technica]]'' stated that "Ubisoft's... plans make no sense" because the Quartz system is so deeply controlled by Ubisoft that a simple conventional internal database would achieve the same result without the overhead of a blockchain.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Orland|first=Kyle|date=8 December 2021|title=Ubisoft's first NFT plans make no sense|url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2021/12/ubisofts-first-nft-plans-make-no-sense/|access-date=9 December 2021|website=Ars Technica}}</ref> Users criticized the technology because Ubisoft terms of service state that the company has "no liability" for claims or damages and is aware that the blockchain "may be subject to specific weaknesses, which make them possibly targets for specific cybersecurity threats" and disclaim "liability in the risks implied by the use of this new technology."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ubisoft's NFT Announcement Has Been Intensely Disliked|url=https://kotaku.com/ubisofts-nft-announcement-has-been-intensely-disliked-1848182203|access-date=9 December 2021|website=Kotaku|date=8 December 2021 }}</ref> On 9 December, Ubisoft de-listed the announcement video on [[YouTube]], following viewer backlash and dislike bombing.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Stanton|first=Rich|date=9 December 2021|title=Ubisoft de-lists overwhelmingly disliked NFT announcement video|work=[[PC Gamer]]|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/uk/ubisoft-de-lists-overwhelmingly-disliked-nft-announcement-video/|access-date=9 December 2021}}</ref> French trade union Solidaires Informatique criticized Ubisoft's plan for Quartz, stating that blockchain technology is "harmful, worthless, and without future", and that it is "a useless, costly, ecologically mortifying tech which doesn't bring anything to videogames".<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2021-12-16-french-trade-union-calls-ubisoft-nft-scheme-a-useless-costly-ecologically-mortifying-technology | title = French trade union criticises Ubisoft Quartz as "a useless, costly, ecologically mortifying tech" | first= Ed | last=  Nightengale | date = 16 December 2021 | accessdate=  16 December 2021 | work = [[Eurogamer]] }}</ref> After their initial release, trade volume for Digits was virtually zero in the following weeks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Subhan |first=Ishraq |date=21 December 2021 |title=Ubisoft appears to have sold a grand total of 15 NFTs |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/ubisoft-appears-to-have-sold-a-grand-total-of-15-nfts |access-date=8 June 2022 |website=Eurogamer}}</ref> Players who used them complained that no one noticed the Digits during multiplayer matches.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Klepek |first=Patrick |date=13 January 2022 |title=We Tracked Down the People Who Are Actually Buying Ubisoft's NFTs |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/we-tracked-down-the-people-who-are-actually-buying-ubisofts-nfts/ |access-date=8 June 2022 |website=Waypoint}}</ref> Ubisoft released the last Digit for Ghost Recon Breakpoint on 17 March 2022 and ended support for the game shortly thereafter.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ubisoft ends Ghost Recon Breakpoint updates, working on NFTs for other titles |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2022-04-06-ubisoft-ends-ghost-recon-breakpoint-development-working-on-nfts-for-other-titles |access-date=6 April 2022 |website=GamesIndustry.biz |date=6 April 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Epps |first=DeAngelo |date=5 April 2022 |title=Ghost Recon Breakpoint support ends months after NFT drop |url=https://www.digitaltrends.com/gaming/ghost-recon-breakpoint-end/ |access-date=8 June 2022 |website=Digital Trends}}</ref>

In December 2021, [[Peter Molyneux]] announced that his development studio [[22cans]]'s planned business simulation game ''Legacy'' would include a cryptocurrency called "LegacyCoin", based on the Ethereum blockchain.<ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.vg247.com/peter-molyneux-blockchain-business-sim-nfts | title = Peter Molyneux is making a blockchain-based business sim with NFTs | first = Jeremy | last =Signor |date = 12 December 2021 | accessdate = 12 December 2021 | work = [[VG247]] }}</ref> Prior to release, speculators could purchase in-game items as NFTs, and sales reached {{USD|50 million|long=no}} within a few days of Molyneux's announcement.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2021-12-16-peter-molyneuxs-nft-game-legacy-has-already-made-usd50m | title = Peter Molyneux's NFT game Legacy has already sold $50m of "land" | first = Tom | last=  Phillips | date = 16 December 2021 | accessdate = 16 December 2021 | work = [[Eurogamer]] }}</ref> That same month, [[GSC Game World]] announced plans to include NFTs in the game ''[[S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2]]''. Due to widespread complaints, a day later the studio announced that they would no longer be pursuing NFTs within the game.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.theverge.com/2021/12/16/22840488/stalker-2-nft-metahuman-gsc-web3-canceled | title = S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2 will no longer have NFTs after fan outcry | first = Jay | last = Peters|  date = 16 December 2021 | accessdate = 16 December 2021 | work =[[The Verge]] }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Wilde|first=Tyler|date=16 December 2021|title=Stalker 2 developer cancels NFT plans following backlash|work=[[PC Gamer]]|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/stalker-2-nft-cancelled/|access-date=17 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Knoop |first1=Joseph |last2=Kim |first2=Matt |title=STALKER 2 Developers Announce They Will No Longer Use NFT [Update] |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/stalker-2-nfts-response |access-date=12 May 2023 |work=IGN |date=16 December 2021 |language=en}}</ref>

In February 2022, games marketplace [[Itch.io]] described NFTs and blockchain games as a "scam", and said that anyone who thought they were useful should "reevaluate your life choices".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Partis |first1=Danielle |title=Itch.io decries NFTs, calls them "a scam" |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/itch-io-decries-nfts-calls-them-a-scam |access-date=9 May 2023 |work=GamesIndustry.biz |date=9 February 2022 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Dinsdale |first1=Ryan |title=Indie Store Itch.io Calls NFTs a Scam: 'Please Re-Evaluate Your Life Choices' |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/indie-store-itchio-nft-scam-please-re-evaluate-your-life-choices |access-date=9 May 2023 |work=IGN |date=7 February 2022 |language=en}}</ref> This announcement was partly in response to an unconfirmed rumor that online publishing platform [[Gumroad]] would become involved with NFTs, which was met with widespread backlash from users.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Vincent |first1=James |title='NFTs are a scam,' says indie game store Itch.io |url=https://www.theverge.com/2022/2/8/22923265/nfts-scam-indie-game-store-itchio-tweet-gumroad |access-date=9 May 2023 |work=The Verge |date=8 February 2022}}</ref>

In July 2022, Mojang Studios announced that NFTs would not be permitted in ''[[Minecraft]]'', saying that "speculative pricing and investment mentality around NFTs takes the focus away from playing the game and encourages profiteering, which we think is inconsistent with the long-term joy and success of our players".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Taylor |first1=Josh |title=Minecraft developers won't allow NFTs on gaming platform |url=https://www.theguardian.com/games/2022/jul/21/minecraft-developers-wont-allow-nfts-on-gaming-platform |access-date=21 July 2022 |work=the Guardian |date=21 July 2022 }}</ref>

[[Will Wright (game designer)|Will Wright]] revealed in October 2022 that his upcoming game ''VoxVerse'' would be a blockchain enabled game. The game's blockchain features were inspired by Wright having seen players in ''[[The Sims]]'' create their own assets and distribute them to others; within ''VoxVerse'', creator players will be able to make areas that other players can explore and interact in, and then trade and sell these assets as NFTs.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.axios.com/2022/10/20/will-wright-voxverse-gala-gallium-blockchain | title = Sims pioneer Will Wright is making a blockchain game, but is down on NFTs  | first= Stephan | last = Tolito | date = October 20, 2022 | accessdate = October 23, 2022 | work = [[Axios (website)|Axios]] }}</ref>

Square Enix committed more to blockchain game support, intending to bring the technology to the ''[[Final Fantasy]]'' series and also announcing new IP named ''Symbiogenesis'' built around NFTs. In a November 2022 investors report, the company said that they consider blockchain technology critical to their growth.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.eurogamer.net/blockchain-technology-key-to-square-enixs-growth-financial-results-show | title = Blockchain technology key to Square Enix's growth, financial results show | first = Ed | last = Nightengale | date = November 7, 2022 | accessdate = November 7, 2022 | work = [[Eurogamer]] }}</ref> Although several other companies had distanced themselves from blockchain and NFT technology following widespread consumer backlash, as of April 2023, Square Enix had reaffirmed its commitment to the technology.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Valentine |first1=Rebekah |title=Square Enix Triples Down on Blockchain With New Deal Even as Other Publishers Flee |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/square-enix-nft-blockchain-web3-elixir |access-date=9 May 2023 |work=IGN |date=19 April 2023 |language=en}}</ref> In February 2025, Square Enix announced it would be ending support for the ''Symbiogenesis'' game.<ref name="Lada-2025">{{cite news |last1=Lada |first1=Jenni |title=Square Enix Will End Symbiogenesis NFT Project, Shares Final Roadmap |url=https://www.siliconera.com/square-enix-will-end-symbiogenesis-nft-project-shares-final-roadmap/ |access-date=26 December 2025 |work=Siliconera |date=21 February 2025}}</ref>

== Reception and criticism ==
[[Xbox]] head executive [[Phil Spencer (business executive)|Phil Spencer]] said in regards to blockchain games "that some of the creative that I see today feels more exploitative than about entertainment".<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.axios.com/xbox-exploitive-nft-gaming-projects-cb3d885f-694c-462d-bcb1-a24c892db32f.html | title =  Xbox chief wary of "exploitive" NFT gaming projects | first = Stephan | last = Tolito | date = 16 November 2021 | accessdate = 17 November 2021 | work = [[Axios (website)|Axios]] }}</ref> When the gaming communication platform [[Discord (software)|Discord]] suggested possible [[Ethereum]] integration into their client in November 2021, users criticized the inclusion of cryptocurrency and Discord backed off, affirming they had no set plans for its inclusion.<ref>{{Cite news|last1=Taylor|first1=Mollie|first2=Tyler |last2=Colp|date=11 November 2021|title=Discord walks back NFT and cryptocurrency plans|work=PC Gamer|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/uk/discord-walks-back-nft-and-cryptocurrency-plans/|access-date=9 December 2021}}</ref>

MMO developer Damion Schubert argued that most pitches for games for NFTs could also be achieved without the use of NFTs and that the non-NFT options would be easier to implement.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Fenlon|first=Wes|date=24 January 2022|title=What to actually expect from NFTs in games this year|work=PC Gamer|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/what-to-actually-expect-from-nfts-in-games-this-year/|access-date=26 January 2022}}</ref>

In November 2021 Rob Fahy wrote in [[Gameindustry.biz]] that the "play-to-earn" business model is similar to earlier systems that encouraged the rise of [[gold farming]] which later led developers to shift to selling "gold" to players directly in real currency. He argued that the business model could potentially reintroduce [[artificial scarcity]] of in-game currency and in-game items or characters, and that in-game marketplaces will likely have a payment system where a game developer takes a cut when players sell a marketplace item to each other.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Baseless NFT hype hits a crescendo – but play-to-earn is worth watching {{!}} Opinion|url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2021-11-05-baseless-nft-hype-hits-a-crescendo-but-its-play-to-earn-thats-worth-watching-opinion|access-date=28 January 2022|website=GamesIndustry.biz|date=5 November 2021 }}</ref>

In December 2021, during [[The Game Awards 2021|The Game Awards]], Josef Fares, director of ''[[It Takes Two (video game)|It Takes Two]]'', stated that he would rather get "shot in the knee" than include NFTs in any of his games.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Grayson|first=Nathan|date=23 December 2021|title=Years after viral Game Awards rant, 'It Takes Two' director says he doesn't hate the Oscars|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/video-games/2021/12/23/josef-fares-it-takes-two-game-awards-interview/|access-date=29 December 2021}}</ref>

Games journalist [[Jason Schreier]] characterised the blockchain "play-to-earn" model as a [[pyramid scheme]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Obedkov |first1=Evgeny |title=Jason Schreier compares business model of blockchain games to pyramid scheme |url=https://gameworldobserver.com/2021/12/14/jason-schreier-compares-business-model-of-blockchain-games-to-pyramid-scheme |access-date=21 January 2022 |work=Game World Observer |date=14 December 2021 |archive-date=21 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220121101415/https://gameworldobserver.com/2021/12/14/jason-schreier-compares-business-model-of-blockchain-games-to-pyramid-scheme |url-status=dead }}</ref> Competing developers of "step-to-earn" games—[[fitness game]]s that reward cryptocurrency for walking—rushed to accuse each other of being [[Ponzi scheme]]s while simultaneously working toward "solutions to their Ponzinomics problem". One developer, StepN, admitted that play-to-earn games require a constant supply of new players or else their token economy would collapse.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Strachan |first=Maxwell |date=8 June 2022 |title=Stepn, 'Move-To-Earn' Games Try To Convince Doubters They're Not Ponzis |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/stepn-move-to-earn-games-try-to-convince-doubters-theyre-not-ponzis/ |access-date=8 June 2022 |website=Motherboard}}</ref>

The [[Game Developers Conference]]'s 2022 annual report stated that 70% of developers surveyed said their studios had no interest in NFTs, while 28% said they were very or somewhat interested in them, and only 1% said they were integrating them into their games. In addition 72% of developers said they were not interested in cryptocurrency as a payment tool for games, while 27% said they were very or somewhat interested, and only 1% saying they were already doing so.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Jeffrey |first1=Cal |date=20 January 2022|title=Game Developers Conference report: most developers frown on blockchain games |url=https://www.techspot.com/news/93075-game-developers-conference-report-indicates-most-developer-frown.html |access-date=21 January 2022 |work=TechSpot}}</ref>

Square Enix's new year letter, which expressed interest in NFTs in video games, received heavy backlash from fans, with many additionally expressing disdain at the letter's comparison of "play to have fun" and "play to contribute" players.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Lang|first=Brad|date=3 January 2022|title=Square Enix's NFT Plans Are Being Roasted Mercilessly by Fans|work=[[Comic Book Resources]]|url=https://www.cbr.com/square-enix-nft-plans-roasted-fans/ |access-date=31 January 2022}}</ref>

===Discontinued games===

* ''[[Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Breakpoint]]'' - Released in 2019 as a non-blockchain game. In 2022, developer [[Ubisoft]] added support for Ubisoft Quartz NFTs. Live support for the game was ended four months later.
* ''Champions Tactics: Grimoria Chronicles'' - Launched in October 2024.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Parrish |first1=Ash |title=Ubisoft dumps its NFT game on the market to little fanfare |url=https://www.theverge.com/2024/10/30/24283677/ubisoft-nft-game-champions-tactics-grimoria-chronicles-sequence |access-date=26 December 2025 |work=The Verge |date=30 October 2024}}</ref> Ubisoft re-released the game as ''Champions Tactics: Reforged'' without blockchain integration.{{cn|date=December 2025}}
* ''Symbiogenesis'' - Launched in December 2023.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Stenbuck |first1=Kite |title=Square Enix Formally Launches NFT Project Symbiogenesis |url=https://www.siliconera.com/square-enix-formally-launches-nft-project-symbiogenesis/ |access-date=26 December 2025 |work=Siliconera |date=21 December 2023}}</ref> Square Enix shut down the servers on July 31, 2025.<ref name="Lada-2025"/>
* ''Captain Tsubasa Rivals'' - Licensed from the ''[[Captain Tsubasa]]'' manga series. KLab Inc. ended support on November 28, 2025.{{cn|date=December 2025}}
* ''The Walking Dead: Empires'' - Licensed from ''[[The Walking Dead (franchise)|The Walking Dead]]'' franchise. Gala Games shut down the servers on July 31, 2025.{{cn|date=December 2025}}
